notes: Market context for 2026-11-17: Monday's tape was a semiconductor-led sell-off (S&P 500 -1.90%, Nasdaq-100 -2.70%, SOX -3.43%) on NVIDIA's leadership vacuum after Jensen Huang's Nov 12 departure plus caution ahead of NVIDIA's fiscal Q3 print AFTER today's close. Today pre-market is a partial reversal: SMH +1.21%, XLK +0.81%, SPY -0.03%, XLV -0.97%. The market's gap book is therefore a policy-driven AI-optical rebound (COHR, AAOI, LITE, MRVL, CRDO, ALAB) plus two clean single-name events (SLS, AS), one earnings withdrawal (RCAT) and two insider/micro-cap bids (PCT, KURA).

The single biggest driver of the ladder is POLICY, not company news: Reuters reported on Nov 17 at 07:32 ET that the US administration is moving ahead with restrictions on imports of new Chinese data-centre optical transceivers, despite lobbying from Amazon, Google, Meta, CoreWeave, Cisco and Microsoft. Coherent, Applied Optoelectronics, Lumentum, Credo and Astera Labs in the ladder are ONE trade expressed several ways, not several setups - and they are the only names in the book with that driver. (Marvell, the acquirer of Lumentum, sits just outside the ladder's own filter on pre-market volume.)
NVIDIA reports after today's close, so the whole AI-connectivity complex is holding a catalyst event overnight. The optical group is levered to that print on top of the export-restriction story.

The Focus book did not fire: 0 of 12 Focus names cleared the 4% / 50,000-share / 25-share gate, and none of them is in the market's ladder. This is structural - the Focus list is the prior session's momentum screen and cannot contain a name whose move has not happened yet. The worst Focus setup was CGON (5 stylists, 7 origins), whose PIVOT-006 win broke on Nov 16 and is already in the price after Monday's +23.7% open.

Reference close discipline: the denominator is the settled 2026-11-16 close carried by the prior sweep's own focus.csv (`today_close`, resolving to the 2026-11-16 session), cross-checked session-exactly against Nasdaq's per-symbol history for 12/12 names with zero conflicts. The sweep's `screen_close_resolved` column belongs to data_date 2026-11-13 and was rejected as a denominator.

Tape freshness: the newest executed print on the Focus tape is 15-27 minutes behind the wall clock for 11 of 12 names; FENC and CPRI are the two stalest (see the Lag column in the Focus scan). Every one of them is BELOW the bar on a thin print, so the staleness does not change a flag - but it is why the Focus scan is a snapshot, not a market.

Two Focus rows are quote artifacts and are named as such in Flags: FOUR (Shift4 Payments) prints +5.93% on the /info quote against a $36.50 x $46.78 band while the executed tape was -0.31% on 100 shares - a quote, not a market; and TNDM's executed tape carried a +10.93% print intraday that is absent from the published PM high/low columns, on a 26-minute-old tape, so treat that excursion as noise.

Catalyst sourcing note: catalysts were confirmed from issuer releases, SEC filings and the wire only. The TradingView `earnings_release_date` field was treated as a candidate, never as a catalyst. Names with no confirmed same-day catalyst are published as 'no catalyst confirmed in this run' - LUCK, TEM, FWDI, RZLV, ACRS, PICS, OXBDF, FUBO and every non-qualifying Focus name.
